# Delta Architecture & Package Boundary Rules
## Overview
Delta is a terminal-based, general-purpose AI assistant. This document establishes strict package boundaries, dependency directions, and architectural invariants to prevent coupling between presentation, application orchestration, agent loop logic, and persistence.
---
## 1. Dependency Graph & Direction
```text cmd/delta (Composition Root) │ ├── internal/config ────────────┐ │ │ ├── internal/core (Orchestrator)─┼── internal/agent (LLM & loop mechanics) │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ├── internal/tool (extensible tool catalog) │ │ │ └── (goai / provider SDK) │ │ │ │ ├─────────────────────────┼── internal/session (durable JSONL storage) │ │ │ │ ├─────────────────────────┼── internal/tools/builtins ── internal/shell │ │ │ │ │ │ └────────────────────────────── internal/workspace │ │ │ └── internal/shell (direct user bash execution) │ └── internal/tui (Bubble Tea adapter & interaction state) │ ├── Bubble Tea v2 / Bubbles ├── internal/workspace (file autocomplete & prompt attachments) └── internal/tui/view (pure deterministic presentation) ```
The dependency direction is strictly one-way: **Presentation (`tui`) -> Application Core (`core`) -> Mechanics / Persistence (`agent`, `session`, `tools/builtins`, `shell`, `workspace`)**.
---
## 2. Package Responsibilities & Ownership
### `cmd/delta` - **Composition Root only.** - Loads configuration (`internal/config`). - Resolves workspace directory. - Instantiates `internal/core.Engine` implementing `core.Backend`. - Initializes `internal/tui.NewAppModel(backend, ...)`. - Starts the Bubble Tea program. - Contains no business logic, no UI rendering, and no direct tool calls.
### `internal/core` - **Application orchestration & backend lifecycle.** - Implements `core.Backend` interface consumed by presentation layers. - Owns the active session lifecycle (create, list, resume, clear). - Coordinates model turns and cancellation contexts. - Owns tool confirmation requests, user approvals, and session-scoped tool allowlists. - Owns slash command discovery and execution registry (`RegisterCommand`, `Commands`, `ExecuteCommand`). - Emits presentation-neutral domain events (`core.Event`) for consumers. - Coordinates persistence with `internal/session`. - **Strict Invariant:** Must NOT import `charm.land/bubbletea`, `charm.land/bubbles`, `charm.land/lipgloss`, or `internal/tui`.
### `internal/agent` - **LLM and tool-loop mechanics.** - Invokes provider SDKs and manages multi-turn tool loops. - Strips reasoning/thought blocks when appropriate. - Executes tool hooks and passes confirmation requests to orchestration bridge. - Emits low-level agent events. - **Strict Invariant:** Must NOT import `internal/session` (agent mechanics do not persist JSONL files).
### `internal/session` - **Durable JSONL session storage.** - Owns JSONL schemas, serialization, and deserialization. - Provides thread-safe, serialized appends to session event streams. - Manages session discovery on disk. - Preserves raw tool arguments and raw output payloads byte-for-byte. - **Strict Invariant:** Does NOT import `internal/tui` or `internal/agent`.
### `internal/tool` - **Extensible tool contracts, descriptors, and policies.** - Defines tool metadata (name, description, display name, confirmation policy). - Defines neutral preview generation (diff lines, command lines) and summaries. - Provides catalog lookup without switch statements. - **Strict Invariant:** Presentation-neutral; does NOT import `charm.land/lipgloss`, `charm.land/bubbletea`, or `charm.land/bubbles`.
### `internal/tools/builtins` - **Concrete built-in tool implementations** (`run_command`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `read_file`, `list_dir`, `search_text`, `find`, `web_fetch`, `schedule`). - Each tool resides in its own cohesive file. - Delegates process execution to `internal/shell` and path safety to `internal/workspace`.
### `internal/shell` - **OS process execution and output capture.** - Single execution point for command execution, timeouts, exit codes, and output streaming. - Shared between `run_command` tool and user interactive Bash mode.
### `internal/workspace` - **Workspace boundaries and filesystem safety.** - Enforces `SafePath` checks including ancestor symlink resolutions to prevent sandbox escapes. - Provides safe workspace file matching (`MatchFiles`) and markdown prompt decoration (`FormatFileContext`, `BuildPromptWithFiles`).
### `internal/config` - Configuration schema, loading, updating, and provider auth resolution.
### `internal/tui` - **Bubble Tea adapter and user interaction state.** - Translates terminal key/mouse events into backend requests. - Maintains terminal viewport, cursor, and scrollback state. - Maps application events (`core.Event`) into presentation models. - **Strict Invariant:** Does NOT import `internal/agent`, `internal/session`, `internal/tools/builtins`, or provider SDKs.
### `internal/tui/view` - **Pure presentation renderers.** - Functions are pure and deterministic mappings: `(data DTOs, dimensions) -> string`. - Never executes I/O, parses raw tool JSON arguments, or communicates with the backend. - **Strict Invariant:** Does NOT import `internal/core`, `internal/agent`, `internal/session`, `internal/tool`, or `internal/tools/builtins`.
---
## 3. Forbidden Patterns & Architectural Invariants
1. **No generic dumping-ground packages:** Do NOT create `internal/utils`, `internal/common`, `internal/misc`, `internal/types`, or `internal/api`. Every type and helper belongs to the package that owns its semantic responsibility. 2. **No backend execution from TUI:** Key handlers in `internal/tui` must never spawn goroutines to run tools, execute shell commands, save sessions, or call provider APIs directly. All actions dispatch via `core.Backend`. 3. **No hard-coded tool switches in UI or View:** Adding a tool must only require registering its descriptor in `internal/tool`. The UI and renderers consume generic previews, display names, and summaries provided by the descriptor. 4. **No fake confirmation options:** Session-scoped approval must record an in-memory session allowlist in `internal/core`, ensuring subsequent invocations in the session do not prompt repeatedly. 5. **No direct persistence from agent:** `internal/agent` produces in-memory turn records and events. Only `internal/core` writes to `internal/session`.
---
## 4. Verification Checklists & Commands
When making changes to Delta, verify the entire test suite and static analysis passes:
### Primary Verification ```bash go test -count=1 ./... && go vet ./... ``` *(Note: On Termux/arm64 environments, `-race` is not supported. Use `-count=1` to disable test caching).*
### Architectural Invariants Check ```bash go test -v -run TestArchitectureImportInvariants ./internal/core ``` This test asserts: - `internal/core` does NOT import `internal/tui`, `charm.land/bubbletea`, `charm.land/bubbles`, or `charm.land/lipgloss`. - `internal/agent` does NOT import `internal/session`. - `internal/tool` does NOT import `charm.land/lipgloss`, `charm.land/bubbletea`, or `charm.land/bubbles`. - `internal/tui/view` does NOT import `internal/core`, `internal/agent`, `internal/session`, `internal/tool`, or `internal/tools`.
### Extensibility Verification (Open-Closed Principle) ```bash go test -v -run TestOCPExtensibility ./internal/core ``` This test verifies: - Registering a new custom slash command dynamically on `core.Engine` updates the command catalog and executes without modifying `internal/tui` or `internal/tui/view`. - Registering a new tool definition in `tool.Registry` generates structured previews, metadata, and summaries without modifying `internal/tui` or `internal/tui/view`.
### Rendering Benchmarks Check ```bash go test -run=^$ -bench=. ./internal/tui/view ```
---
## 5. Regression Rules for Future Contributors
1. **Adding a Slash Command:** Add a `CommandDescriptor` in `internal/core/commands.go` (or register it via `Engine.RegisterCommand`). Never add command branching inside `internal/tui/view` or `internal/tui/model.go`. 2. **Adding a New Tool:** Implement the tool in `internal/tools/builtins` and declare its `tool.Definition` in `internal/tool`. Supply its `DisplayName`, `Summarize`, and `Confirmation` generators. Never add `switch toolName` statements in `internal/tui` or `internal/tui/view`. 3. **Modifying Views:** Keep all view rendering functions pure: `(DTOs, width) -> string`. Do not make network calls, read files, or parse raw JSON strings inside `internal/tui/view`. 4. **Extending Event Streams:** Add new event variants to `core.Event` in `internal/core/events.go`. Ensure events carry self-contained presentation-neutral metadata. 5. **Session Replay Fidelity:** Ensure any event serialized to JSONL preserves the raw inputs and outputs necessary to accurately reconstruct conversation context upon `/resume`.

BINARY_NAME := bin/delta MAIN_SRC := ./cmd/delta/main.go GO := go
.PHONY: all build run test clean tidy fmt vet lint
all: build
build: @mkdir -p bin $(GO) build -o $(BINARY_NAME) $(MAIN_SRC)
run: build ./$(BINARY_NAME)
test: $(GO) test -v ./...
tidy: $(GO) mod tidy
fmt: $(GO) fmt ./...
vet: $(GO) vet ./...
lint: vet @echo "Lint checks passed (go vet)."
check: fmt vet test
clean: rm -rf bin/
